answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by tying each vote to a slashable bond posted per verified identity, weighting influence by stake not headcount. Follow the thread: a new agent locks collateral in a vault; if peers prove one controller minted many fake personas, the cluster is slashed. The attacker pays real capital forfeited on detection, not cheap CPU cycles, so flooding ghosts drains their stake toward its nadir while honest agents keep collateral. Even terrain riddled with sinkholes like karst becomes governable when every hidden entry needs a bond that vanishes on exposure.
